bullets.title: NVDA: In early talks to acquire/invest in Reflection AI (~$25B); halting RTX 5090 for data center GPUs
bullets.body: NVDA is in early-stage talks to acquire or deepen investment in Reflection AI (open-weight model developer) at ~$25B, potentially via acqui-hire to sidestep regulatory scrutiny—helping NVDA build an integrated AI stack and defend against hyperscaler custom ASICs. Separately, NVDA is halting RTX 5090 production to prioritize higher-margin AI data center and professional GPUs. NBIS fell ~2.6% on read-throughs from the Reflection AI deal reports.

bullets.title: AMZN: In talks to acquire Decart AI for ~$7B to boost Trainium adoption vs. NVDA
bullets.body: Amazon is in discussions to acquire AI startup Decart for approximately $7B (75% premium to its $4B May valuation); Decart's chip-switching technology would make it easier for AWS customers to migrate from NVDA to Amazon's Trainium chips. The deal also positions AWS more broadly in the agentic AI chip-agnostic market.

bullets.title: CRM: BofA double-upgrade to Buy; acquires AI analytics platform Loops
bullets.body: BofA upgraded CRM to Buy from Sell (double upgrade) after the stock fell ~11% since Sept 1 vs software +7%; CRM was up 4.7% premarket on the news. Additionally, Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Loops, an AI-powered business analytics platform, expected to close early November FY27 with undisclosed terms.

bullets.title: ADBE: Wells Fargo double-downgrades to Underweight, cuts PT to $225 (7% downside)
bullets.body: Wells Fargo downgraded ADBE to Underweight from Overweight and cut the price target to $225 from $270, implying ~7% downside from current levels. ADBE was trading down ~2.9% premarket. FactSet consensus PT stands at $272.

bullets.title: HUBS: Barclays downgrades to Equal Weight; executing 7% workforce reduction
bullets.body: Barclays downgraded HUBS to Equal Weight from Overweight, maintaining a $240 PT (~5% upside). Separately, HUBS is executing a 7% workforce reduction (~660 roles) with $65-75M in charges while reaffirming FY26 guidance. Wolfe notes HUBS is approaching a local valuation minimum at ~15x FCF CY28 ex-SBC.

bullets.title: FSLR: Truist upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $270 (52% upside)
bullets.body: Truist upgraded First Solar to Buy from Hold and raised its price target to $270 from $229, implying ~52% upside from $177.82. FSLR was up 3.3% in premarket. FactSet average target is $280.70.

bullets.title: MSFT, PLTR, SNOW: Phillip Securities downgrades all three
bullets.body: Phillip Securities downgraded MSFT to Neutral from Accumulate with a $515 PT (implying ~4% downside), PLTR to Neutral from Buy with a $215 PT (~3% upside), and SNOW to Accumulate from Buy with a $423 PT (~15% upside). PANW was also cut to Neutral.

bullets.title: TSM: Earnings Thu 10/15; expected sixth straight record quarter; 2027 capex key debate
bullets.body: TSM is expected to hit the high end of Q3 guidance or beat slightly on iPhone 18 and AI server demand, with Q4 gross margins seen flat Q/Q at ~66.4%. The key debate is 2027+ capex guidance—GS estimates $60-64B CY26 capex (up 47-57% YoY) rising to ~$77B in CY27. September revenue was already +55% YoY. Buyside is trimming semis ahead of prints on over-ownership concerns despite bullish AI narrative.

bullets.title: MU/SNDK: Memory under pressure from China CXMT progress; HBF seen as $40-150B TAM by 2030
bullets.body: MU and SNDK each fell ~2% premarket as China's CXMT reported progress on 4F² DRAM architecture and already holds ~10% global DRAM share with a server product targeted by end-2026. GS flagged High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) as a potential AI inference cost reducer (~30%) with a $40-150B TAM by 2030—SNDK and SK Hynix are preferred HBF beneficiaries while MU is a less direct play. Memory/HDD was the most net-sold segment last week.

bullets.title: MRVL: PT raised to $450 (from $325) at Jefferies; FY31 revenue target lifted to $80B
bullets.body: Following MRVL's Analyst Day, Jefferies raised its PT to $450 from $325 on a new F31 framework—interconnect at $37.5B, custom silicon ~$30B, switching/storage ~$10B—with C28 EPS of $13.42. F28 revenue raised to ~$20B, reaching the F29 target one year early on scale-up optics and switching strength. MRVL is confident in holding DSP share vs AVGO.

bullets.title: IREN: +4-5% on multiyear cloud deal with Anthropic
bullets.body: IREN signed a multiyear cloud services deal with Anthropic, sending shares up 4-5% in premarket trading. HUT was also flagged by Piper as a key partner for Louisiana data center buildout with another deal potentially announced after midterms.

bullets.title: NFLX: Most Crowded Short in Internet & Media heading into Q3 earnings; engagement problem persists
bullets.body: JPM characterizes NFLX as the Most Crowded Short in Internet & Media entering Q3 earnings. Management acknowledges growth is slower than desired; investors expect no beat and minimal raises. Q3 revenue is seen +11% YoY in line with guidance, and any Q4/2026 guide-down will not be tolerated. The 2027 revenue growth debate: bears see <10% risk, bulls ~11%; Hedgeye flags NFLX remains in a bearish trend.

bullets.title: AAPL: JPM raises PT to $360; iPhone 18 ASP +15% YoY but Pro component orders cut 15%
bullets.body: JPM raised its AAPL PT to $360 from $340, forecasting F4Q26 revenue of $112.9B (+10% YoY) with iPhone ASP ~$1,000 (+15% YoY). However, multiple sources flagged that Apple cut iPhone 18 Pro component orders by at least 15% amid soft demand while raising Pro Max orders 10-15%. FY27/FY28 EPS raised to $9.50/$10.60. The volume cuts are characterized as normal cycle adjustments, not demand concerns.

bullets.title: ENPH: Losing residential market share to Tesla Powerwall 3 on $1,500-2,000 price premium
bullets.body: ROTH channel checks reveal a California-based ENPH-focused installer has shifted volume primarily to Tesla PW3 due to ENPH's $1,500-2,000 pricing premium. ENPH needs to lower prices to recapture share. The broader US residential solar market faces FEOC/domcon complexity, financing uncertainty, and 25D tax credit loss headwinds, with one installer reporting 30% YTD installation declines and 40-50% y/y sales declines.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini 4 'Carbon' internally competitive with Claude Opus 5.5; Hedgeye turns bullish
bullets.body: Multiple sources report GOOGL employees are upbeat on Gemini 4 'Carbon' currently in internal testing, describing it as competitive with Anthropic's Opus 5.5 on coding tasks. Separately, Hedgeye shifted GOOGL from bearish to bullish trend signal. MS expects agentic AI to shift $22-55B of lodging marketing spend from OTAs, with GOOGL currently capturing $40-55B—a structural headwind for its search/travel vertical.

bullets.title: META: Muse agent reshaping agentic commerce; 'Watermelon' product launch imminent
bullets.body: META's Muse personal AI agent (launched Sept 8) is driving early agentic commerce adoption—Forter data shows Muse accounted for over 50% of agentic orders on its network in the first week of detection; retail is 35% of agent-facilitated transactions. A new 'Watermelon' product launch is described as imminent by Zuckerberg. Meta is beta-testing direct checkout in Muse with Adyen, PayPal, Stripe, and Shopify.

bullets.title: AMD: Helios rack ramp bullish for ANET, CLS, HPE; CPU price hikes of ~10% incoming
bullets.body: AMD's Helios switching tray drew strong attention at the OCP show (100% sold out); Wolfe is bullish on Celestica, Arista, and HPE as ecosystem beneficiaries. AMD is also extending Taiwan investment beyond its $10B May commitment with C27 capacity to 'substantially increase.' On pricing, AMD and Intel are raising CPU prices (~10% and 15-20% respectively) due to higher TSMC foundry costs.

bullets.title: NOW: Expected to beat on CC cRPO growth and AI SKU adoption; Jefferies bullish into print
bullets.body: Jefferies expects NOW to beat on current-quarter contracted remaining performance obligation (CC cRPO) growth and subscription revenue driven by AI SKU adoption. 76% of VARs saw pipeline growth in FQ3; none saw decline for the first time in 11 quarters. Cyber stocks broadly trading at peak multiples with cloud security as the top NTM IT investment priority.

bullets.title: BABA: JPM maintains OW, raises PT to $200 on December-quarter cloud profitability crossover
bullets.body: JPM cut FY27/28E non-GAAP EPS by 9-10% on higher infrastructure costs but raised FY27E EBITDA by 8% and PT to $200 USD/HK$195 (17x FY28E P/E). The thesis: cloud EBITA will exceed AI model losses for the first time in the December quarter, enabling cloud growth to contribute positively to group earnings. JPM remains 14%/30% above consensus on FY27/28 EBITDA and would add into the print.

bullets.title: CEG, TLN, VST: Nuclear/power names surging on AI power demand; weekly leaders
bullets.body: CEG rose 12.2% on a 20-year Google power deal and TLN rose 18% WoW on DOE nuclear loan news. VST added 15.3% WoW. The 'Coiled Springs' power basket (CEG, TLN, VST, AEP, ETR, NEE) delivered 4.3% weekly excess return vs 1.4% for other utilities. MS projects a 32GW net US data center power shortfall through 2028, supporting the multi-year power scarcity theme.
